description: A full repository scan establishes absence. A current scanned verification site or active typed verification binding satisfies this check under the existing verification model. The finding is derived at scan time. Active status remains valid before implementation, even when the configured policy reports a finding.
statement: The coverage check reports each active Rule that has no current verification binding.

description: In Ben’s example, a comment on a platform-support Rule asks for Bun support. The new obligation shares the cited Rule’s Requirement and appears as a sibling. Do not make the cited Rule its parent or place it at the document root solely because it came from discussion. Selection among multiple containing Requirements remains open.
statement: An additional Rule from a cited Rule defaults to the same containing Requirement.

description: The record kind is added when the ids match across kinds; an uncontested title shows nothing. Verified by property including chip minimality. Amended 2026-08-10: enforcement is now genuinely per page - one renderer sees every titled link a page renders, including decision titles, citations, and classification rows, so cross-section collisions get chips.
statement: Two links sharing a title but meaning different records each show the shortest ending of their id that tells them apart, never fewer than eight characters

name: Anchor resolves before site classification

description: Identical content passes; records behind no assertion change freely. Two readings of cited: a contribution through the claim ids an assertion supports, a synthesis packet by the id it names - both are uses of one shared core, so the freeze cannot drift between kinds. Import hand-derives the same freeze and drifted on deletion (tracked in beads).
statement: A record cited by an assertion cannot be replaced with different content

statement: A record cited by an assertion cannot be deleted

description: Repository configuration selects warning or error severity for the lifecycle binding findings. Warnings appear in the report without causing command failure. Error findings appear in the report and cause a nonzero exit. Rule severity metadata is a separate field and does not itself select the command result.
statement: The coverage check reports warning findings without failure and fails when an error finding occurs.

description: The ids go to the database in chunks of 500, since one statement binds a bounded number of parameters. The ids are sorted and deduplicated before chunking, so an id that repeats across two chunks is still one row, and the answer is in id order.
statement: A lookup by ids answers a repeated id once

description: Resolved and archived threads never win, and a record with no active thread has no canonical thread. Verified by property over generated thread lists with deliberate ties. The live path in thread_writers also archives the losing active siblings; that archiving is now rule_thread_siblings_archived, marked and property-verified. Supersedes imported rule PROV-IDEATE-032 jointly with rule_thread_siblings_archived: concurrent posting on one parent must leave exactly one active thread.
statement: choose_canonical_active_thread picks the oldest active thread as canonical, breaking created_at ties by lower id

name: Add the matching SDK exactly
description: The command uses Cargo's @=version requirement syntax against the selected package; real Cargo acceptance, not a fake argument parser, is required evidence.

name: Mutate the selected package manifest
description: The cargo add command receives the selected manifest path. It does not ask Cargo to resolve the selected package name again.
statement: Cargo init passes the selected package manifest path to cargo add without resolving the package name again.

description: Compatible registry requirements and explicit path or Git development overrides are preserved, including workspace-inherited dependencies and active Cargo patches. An incompatible registry requirement fails before manifest, lockfile, or Provenance state mutation.
statement: Cargo initialization changes the provenance-sdk dependency only when the selected package has no existing declaration

name: Guarded Cargo pair rollback
description: The pair coordinator compares both files with their observed post-Cargo bytes, presence, and permissions before writing either. It then restores the manifest before the lockfile. If lockfile restoration fails, it attempts to compensate the manifest to its post-Cargo state. Concurrent edits and restoration or compensation failures are returned with their causes. The coordinator does not claim a crash-wide or filesystem-atomic outcome.
statement: On a handled post-Cargo failure, Cargo init validates both observed file states before attempting pair restoration and reports every concurrent edit, restoration failure, or compensation failure

name: Select one workspace package
description: The default is available only for one eligible workspace member. An explicit package name must identify an eligible workspace member.
statement: Cargo init selects the sole workspace package by default and requires --package when more than one workspace package is eligible.

name: Use the selected package directory
description: The default scope path is relative to the workspace root and points to the selected package directory.
statement: Cargo init uses the selected package directory as the default scope path prefix.

name: Emit the Cargo init next step
description: The directive contains one stable instruction for the project initializer.
statement: The provenance-cli build script emits 'cargo:warning=Next step: run cargo provenance init in your project.'

name: Use only the sibling CLI
description: The shim does not search PATH for a fallback provenance executable. It forwards init arguments and preserves the sibling process exit status.
statement: cargo-provenance runs only the sibling provenance executable and returns its exit status.

description: Catch-up and rebuild hash the repository state tree through a store that borrows the publication guard. Neither pass copies the state tree.
statement: Catch-up reads canonical state in place under the publication guard.
source_section: C. In-place hashing (items 1 and 2), C.3 Byte identity of answers

description: Catch-up and rebuild hash each changed unit before and after parsing. A mismatch discards that parse. After three failed attempts the pass refuses and commits nothing. A read with an existing projection reports catch_up_failed at the stored serial.
statement: Catch-up stores the digest of the bytes it parsed.
source_section: C. In-place hashing (items 1 and 2), C.3 Byte identity of answers

description: A changed scope runs graph and ideation validation. A changed global unit validates every manifest scope. An unchanged scope is not parsed. A validation failure commits no projection change.
statement: Catch-up validates only changed scopes unless the global unit changes.
source_section: C. In-place hashing (items 1 and 2), C.3 Byte identity of answers

description: There are exactly two viewing states for a change. Before shows the earlier version and After shows the resulting version. After is the normal view. Switching views does not save, cancel or undo an edit. Source citation and revision behaviour follow the existing lifecycle.
statement: The change viewer switches between Before and After, with After as the normal view.

description: The dual of rule_claim_eligibility: entry and exit guard the same set of statuses, proven by an exhaustion test asserting claim_survives equals no-blocking-status over all six ShapingStatus values. Written independently of the eligibility predicate so the duality proof is not vacuous.
statement: A claim does not survive its record leaving the claimable state: closing a topic, answering a question, or blocking it on a human clears the claim

description: One decision over both status enums; the refusal names the state with the word the record stores. Proven exhaustively over all six statuses. The dual is rule_claim_cleared_on_exit, extracted 2026-08-10 with an exhaustion proof that entry and exit agree exactly. Review note 2026-08-10: the eligibility check now runs before proposal surfacing, so a closed topic in a scope with a corrupt proposal shard reports the closure rather than the parse error - a deliberate error-order change.
statement: Shaping work may be claimed only while its record is open for work: a closed topic, or an answered or human-blocked question, cannot be claimed
The CLI serves the compiled review page assets.

description: Use the existing origin_thread and origin_message fields for Requirements and Rules. Keep discussion origin separate from the refinement relation selected for tree placement. This records the accepted link from discussion to its resulting record.
statement: A record created from a comment links to that comment as its origin.

description: The person can choose another valid Requirement in the tree. A new Requirement uses its refines relation; a new Rule uses its requirement_ids relation. Default placement follows a compatible cited item, otherwise the root of the viewed document, as stated in rule_comment_outcome_default_attachment.
statement: A person can select the Requirement that a comment-created record refines.

description: The actions start from the selected comment in the record discussion. Existing Provenance record types and relations apply.
statement: Each comment provides actions to create a Requirement or Rule.

description: Follow the starting comment citation to an item that supports a valid attachment for the new record type. Prefer that item over the root of the currently viewed document. This applies to initial selection; the person can choose another valid target. Never treat the global graph root as the document root. Ambiguous citations or an incompatible document root remain detailed design work.
statement: A comment-created record defaults to a compatible cited item, or otherwise to the document root.

description: A person can search for and choose another attachment in the tree. Compatibility follows the existing relation rules for the new record type. Refinement, Resolution production and discussion origin remain separate relations.
statement: The parent picker finds compatible attachment targets through fuzzy search.

description: The dialog lets the person review and change the proposed content and placement before submission. The document reflects the new item after submission. This governs the document interaction; storage of temporary drafts and failed submissions remains a design detail.
statement: A comment-created record enters the document only after submission of its editable creation dialog.

description: The cache pool runs SQLite in WAL mode and holds one connection. A pool of one closes once, so SQLite takes the exclusive lock at close and runs the checkpoint that removes the two files. A pool that grew to two connections closed them at once and left the files behind about half the time.
statement: A completed read leaves no -wal or -shm file beside the cache database

description: Channel split, deliberate: the graph channel rejects the record; the annotation channel warns on the line and falls back to the default 1.0. The two agree on the verdict and differ only in the remedy - a conformance test holds the scanner to core's verdict on generated values. Silent clamping was removed at conversion.
statement: A confidence is a real number between zero and one; out-of-range values are never silently repaired
A change to text, severity, placement or citations requires a new review decision.

description: Identity includes operation, repository, scope, filters and ordering. Authorization is checked again for each request. Invalid or mismatched cursors are refused.
statement: A continuation cursor applies only to its original query.

description: The refusal identifies a required restart. No page from the new revision is appended to the old result.
statement: A continuation request refuses a changed graph revision.

description: Show the earlier and resulting text of the change associated with the discussion through the Before/After viewer. A link to the latest record alone can lose that context after later edits.
statement: A discussion outcome for an updated record shows the change from its previous text.

description: Actor ids are audit attestations under repository access, not cryptographic identity proof. The default manifest ships an empty allowlist, which blocks every disposition (tracked in beads). Proven over the powerset of a two-actor universe crossed with the disposing actor and disposition presence.
statement: Only an actor listed in the repository manifest may dispose of a live proposal

description: Four conditions judged on loaded scope state by a pure function; write_disposition is load, judge, write under the lifecycle lock. Rejected and deferred decisions need no assertion. Proven over 108 points with a real artifact index, plus one example per refusal arm. Convergence with core's validate_disposition_links is recommended and tracked in beads. Amended 2026-08-10: an accepted disposition needs a prior assertion UNLESS its actor is human and it names a canonical artifact - a ratified tournament decision stands in for the swarm's assertion. Proven over 324 cases including the identity axis. Supersedes imported rule PROV-IDEATE-003, which asked that persona comments, synthesis, and proposal cards never become canonical records unless a human accepts the proposal.
statement: A disposition is written only when its proposal exists and is undisposed, any named artifact exists in the scope, and an accepting decision follows an assertion or a human's ratified canonical artifact

description: The published page list is the authority, not the filesystem. Deliberately out of scope: bare anchors, absolute paths, any URL scheme, non-md destinations, trailing fragments, and images. Reference-style links are covered (pulldown-cmark resolves them to the same tag); image destinations are not seen. Parser-option asymmetry between check and serve is tracked in beads.
statement: A markdown link naming a local document must resolve to a page the docs site publishes

description: Heading levels follow the document structure, as with H1, H2 and H3. This changes heading scale, not the reading width. Exact sizes remain prototype details.
statement: Document heading size decreases with record nesting depth.

description: Records with no domain group as Unassigned rather than being dropped, so nothing vanishes from the wiki. Rule-to-requirement attribution is single-homed: one forward pass builds the inverse map both the domains page and the rule page read. Verified by property over generated requirement trees, including refines_into cycles.
statement: A requirement belongs to its own domain and every domain of its parents, and a rule to every domain of the requirements behind it

description: After dispatch, response loss, timeout, malformed responses, and interruption cannot establish rollback. Session memory retains the unresolved attempt until the application obtains independent evidence. No automatic replacement mutation is sent.
statement: The Effect SDK retains an unresolved mutation outcome when completion is unknown.
source_document: Bead provenance-7pkm, user dispatch of 11 September 2026
source_section: Acceptance criterion 4 and Scenario: Lose a mutation result

statement: The evidence answer carries one has_more flag for each of its four lists beside the top-level flag

description: Apply this interaction to existing document items. Free-text editing should feel like working in a Markdown document. New item creation continues to use the agreed dialog. This Rule does not choose autosave or commit timing.
statement: Clicking an editable field opens its editor in place.

description: Twelve field sites (sources, requirements, resolutions, rules x origin thread/message; topics, questions x claimed by/at) are written once in visit_collaboration_fields; stripping and rejecting are two uses of the same walk, so the lists cannot drift. Proven per field site with coverage derived by running the real walk, plus a property that strip-then-validate always passes over all 4096 site subsets.
statement: A graph shared outside the repository carries no collaboration fields: export clears them and import rejects them through one shared field walk

description: The failure may be a validator refusal or an I/O error. The error text travels beside the answer in freshness_error. A cache directory the process cannot write opens as an immutable image, so a read-only checkout answers at the serial it holds.
statement: A failed freshness step over a stored revision answers at that serial with the policy word catch_up_failed

description: One count predicate behind three flag families (resolution inputs, canonical artifact pair, source ref clause); refusal wording stays at each site. Proven exhaustively over count tuples against an oracle that derives the record count from the maximum rather than the first flag. The proposals handler's target pair now routes through the same predicate, and blank input content is refused by rule_resolution_input_content.
statement: A flag family naming part of a record must name all of it: required flags appear once per record, optional flags are omitted entirely or appear once per record
The freshness flag takes precedence over the settings file, which takes precedence over the default catch_up policy.

name: The gate classifies, it does not review
statement: The diff gate classifies an evidence path as untouched, touched, moved, or gone, and performs no review and no re-extraction

description: Differently-spelled git patterns are deliberately treated as different patterns; matching them would need pattern semantics and risk silently not ignoring the directory. Existing lines, including duplicates, remain byte-identical. An unreadable .gitignore propagates its error instead of being treated as empty.
statement: A generated output directory gets one matching ignore line when none exists, and repeated calls never add another matching line

description: The endpoint can be local or hosted. The native Rust SDK is a separate open product question.
statement: Generated SDKs invoke engine operations through HTTP.
source_section: U8-A8-U9: all generated SDKs use HTTP, with endpoint and credential configuration.

description: The gap kinds: a requirement with no domain, no source refs, no resolving decision, or no produced rules; a rule missing either producer (owner ruling 2026-08-10: full tracing needs BOTH a producing requirement and a producing resolution; the gap names the missing end); a resolution resolving nothing; a source nothing references; a reference to a record that does not exist; an unresolved contradicts pair; an open question; an unexplored topic. Single seam consumed by the gaps command, prime, and the wiki assembler.
statement: compute_gaps decides what counts as an unfinished spot in a graph; a complete chain from source to rule with settled topics and questions yields no gaps

description: The guard owns its repository layout. Guarded stores and state snapshots derive their layout from the guard. Callers cannot supply another layout. The owner required this correction in PR 198.
statement: Guarded stores and state snapshots use the repository layout of their publication guard.
source_section: C.2 The pass after items 1 and 2, item 2; C.3 Byte identity of answers

description: Ask the person for a ticket whose structure they like. Reuse an available desired schema without asking for another example.
statement: When no ticket schema is available, the agent asks for a link to an example ticket.

description: Record the reusable shape for later task generation. Ticket schema means the person’s desired fields and structure; no fixed tracker-specific format or new Provenance record type is selected.
statement: The agent derives the desired ticket schema from the supplied example ticket.

description: The agent decomposes shaped Requirements into tasks for the person. Use the recorded ticket schema and available tools for the chosen destination. This product decision does not send tickets now or authorize unrelated external writes.
statement: The agent writes derived tasks to the user’s chosen issue tracker or Markdown.

description: Hosts supply storage and hosting context. They do not own separate copies of operation behavior.
statement: Local and hosted HTTP handlers call the same Rust operation implementation.
source_section: U7: local and remote logic use the same core package. U8-U9 and U12: accepted arrangement.

description: Enforced by construction: the predicate has one home in ids.rs and an invalid id is unrepresentable as a StableId or ScopeId (private fields, no bypassing impls, hand-written Deserialize routing through the constructor). All four shipped JSON-schema patterns agree with the runtime on a 50-value boundary corpus, verified by conformance against the emitted schemas. DispositionActor.id is deliberately outside the rule (actor identity, not a graph id).
statement: Every id in the graph is non-empty and uses only lowercase letters, digits, underscore, or hyphen
Impact follows each declared relation in its flow direction for at most ten steps and adds no other step
The impact answer says scan_cut when its file scan stopped short

description: Both primary implementation and verification bindings are checked. Deprecated or archived Rules with no current bindings do not trigger this finding. Markers that cite an id with no Rule record produce an unknown-id warning.
statement: The coverage check reports current implementation or verification bindings to deprecated or archived Rules.

name: Roll back owned init changes
description: Rollback compares each current target with the state written by this application. It restores matching targets in reverse order, preserves concurrent edits, and reports every failed restoration.
statement: On a handled InitPlan application failure, init restores each file or link that still matches the state written by that application.

name: Use supported graph write paths
statement: The generated AGENTS.md permits graph writes only through the Provenance CLI or SDK and forbids direct edits to .provenance/state

name: Require grounded statement writing
statement: The generated AGENTS.md tells agents to use provenance-grounded-writing before they write or change a Requirement or Rule statement

description: The shared repository initializer supplies this behavior to plain provenance init and Cargo init; reruns do not alter already current skill files.
statement: Every successful provenance init installs the bundled Provenance skills in the repository

name: Keep managed paths in the repository
description: Planning and application inspect the .agents and .claude ancestor paths without following symbolic links. A refused path is not written outside the repository.
statement: Init refuses a managed onboarding target when a path component below the repository root is a symbolic link.

name: Keep native commands valid
statement: Native initialization writes commands that use the installed Provenance executable

description: The projection owns only the exact ## Provenance heading. Renamed headings remain unchanged. When the exact heading is absent, init appends the ratified section. Before this projection, a separate cleanup removes only legacy blocks whose content hash proves ownership. Repeated initialization is byte-for-byte idempotent.
statement: After legacy cleanup, the heading projection preserves AGENTS.md content outside the exact Provenance section.

name: Planning rejection preserves targets
description: Publication recovery and cache coordination occur before initialization planning. The preservation baseline is the recovered repository. Planning rejection makes no further changes to initialization targets. This guarantee does not claim crash-wide transactionality after apply begins.
statement: A rejected initialization plan leaves its targets unchanged from their state after publication recovery.

name: Complete initialization plan
description: The plan stores observed target state and final regular-file bytes. Apply rechecks those observations before it executes the classified actions.
statement: Before its first onboarding target write, Init classifies the planned manifest, canonical and Claude skills, legacy cleanup, AGENTS.md, and .gitignore

name: Limit statement-check claims
statement: The generated AGENTS.md says that a clean statement report covers only implemented Issue 9 checks and does not prove full conformance

name: Require statement preflight
statement: The generated AGENTS.md tells agents to run the shared Rust statement checker before each Requirement or Rule graph write

name: Use the project TypeScript engine
statement: TypeScript initialization writes commands that use the installed project package and do not select a global Provenance executable

name: Upgrade hash-owned skills
description: A newer stamp, a same-version stamp with different content, a malformed semantic version, an edited payload, or an unstamped file is foreign content. Init preserves foreign content and reports the standalone force option.
statement: Init replaces a stamped skill only when its stamp has an older semantic version and its hash matches its payload.

name: Validate planned repository
description: An existing state tree uses the normal publication lock, recovery, and path containment before planned validation reads it. Validation of a new repository stays read-only because no canonical state exists yet.
statement: Init validates the planned Manifest and disposition actor allowlist against the publication-coordinated existing graph before it writes initialization targets.

description: One classification (target state x identical/different x force) with three shells reading the filesystem in their own terms - file bytes, symlink target, directory tree. Proven over all 8 state x force calls against an independent oracle: nothing the install did not write is destroyed without force, and force changes nothing where the user has nothing at stake.
statement: Installing a skill never replaces something already at the target path unless force is passed; an identical install is a no-op

description: Nothing branches on the answer - it is the one line a reader takes as the account of the run, so it must never claim more or less than happened. Proven over the powerset of per-file outcome kinds, with order- and multiplicity-invariance checked rather than assumed.
statement: A skills install run is reported updated when any file changed, installed when files were only added, and unchanged otherwise

description: A migration that recreates tables commits before the rebuild that refills them. The migration transaction deletes every unit and family digest row, so a crash between the two leaves a database whose next pass re-derives every family, instead of one whose digests claim rows that are not there.
statement: A catch-up pass after an interrupted migration rebuild reloads every family
source_section: store: a migration forgets the digests, so a crash before its rebuild heals

statement: An invalid read setting causes a typed settings refusal before the query reads the projection.

description: Anything the user touched is left alone: a single changed byte in the frontmatter or payload fails the hash and preserves the file. The version inside the header line is intentionally outside the hash, so a version bump alone does not orphan a file. The AGENTS.md marker block shares the proof core (hash_proves_ownership) but is a sibling decision without its own rule yet.
statement: A legacy skill file is deleted only when its embedded hash proves it is byte-for-byte what provenance installed

description: This gate is the admission half; the byte freeze is the SHA-256 fingerprint in core legacy_validation. Known bypass tracked in beads: the gate reads the proposal's current state, so a coordinated row-plus-flip write walks through - which is exactly how commit ac661a2 broke the frozen digests. The missing half is frozen-audit membership, and nothing refuses writes to the retired shard at write time. Amended 2026-08-10: admission now requires frozen-audit membership (the whole set must hash to the shipped disposition digest), closing the coordinated row-plus-state bypass; the left-proposed check remains as an honest superset.
statement: The retired promotion_decisions shard admits a row only when its proposal has already left proposed; it may hold only the shipped audit, never a new decision

description: Saving a graph edit makes it available in the default local review view without a Git commit. Existing Provenance source, revision, and lifecycle behavior still applies. This Rule does not specify updates for unsaved editor content.
statement: The default local reviewer displays saved, uncommitted graph edits.

name: Missing recorded file is stale, not retired
statement: A binding whose recorded file no longer exists is surfaced by the stale gate and is not retired

description: Native entry points use the shared operation behavior. Local MCP does not need an HTTP server for these calls.
statement: The bundled CLI and local MCP call shared Rust operations directly.
source_section: U7-U8: bundled CLI can execute native Rust. U11-A11-U12: local MCP follows the same native path.

description: The relations table is one row per owner, relation, and target, while a requirement citing one source under two clauses stores two references. The core dedupes after its sort, so the served operations, prime, gaps, wiki, and the impact command agree. This is derivation entry 1.
statement: A record's neighbors hold one entry per relation, direction, and endpoint
The nested document view has no separate outline panel.

description: The macro validates the literal from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR and passes that package-resolved candidate to provenance-store; the existing store-owned resolution Rule governs repository normalization.
statement: implemented_by resolves its package-relative file literal against the Cargo package manifest directory
The store refuses a new contribution or synthesis packet whose target names no record in its scope.

description: These actions apply to each new proposed item. Question opens discussion while the approval decision remains open.
statement: A new item offers Approve, Reject and Question actions.

description: This holds under every freshness policy: an absent database file, a file from before the revision tables, and a failed catch-up over either. The refusal is typed as ReadRefusal::NoProjection and carries the freshness error when there is one.
statement: A read with no stored revision refuses and names provenance materialize

name: No stored verified status
statement: No verified status is stored. A rule is unverified when it has neither a live scanned verification site nor an active verification binding
A stored ideation target that names no record is a dangling-reference gap, not a refusal.
source_section: H. Dangling-target existence validation for ideation targets

description: The source language and generation mechanism are not selected by this Rule.
statement: The published operation contract is generated from code.

description: Dot, dot-dot, empty segments, backslashes, and control characters are refused by name, so a hostile or buggy route cannot escape the staged output directory. classify_route is the single authority on acceptance and decomposition; the writer only maps its verdict to an error. Deliberate tightening at conversion: routes with empty segments were previously repaired silently and are now refused. Review note 2026-08-10: a drive-letter segment like C: is accepted as a plain name; harmless on the unix target the writer runs on, noted for any future Windows staging.
statement: A generated page is written only to a route bounded by slashes whose every segment is a plain name

description: Enforced by construction: GraphExport has no fields for proposals, assertions, dispositions, contributions, packets, or threads, and deny_unknown_fields refuses a returning document that names one. The rule marker sits on the struct because only the type governs both directions. The Value-typed escape hatches (expression/inputs/review_triggers) were deleted outright on 2026-08-10, closing the leak route.
statement: Only the canonical graph families travel in a pinned graph; collaboration and ideation records never enter the projection

description: A pinned graph names one scope; its digest and counts are read as facts about that scope alone, so a single stray record would smuggle another scope's data into a handover. The first offending record is named in the refusal. Proven per record family (11 families), with the family list tied to the GraphExport shape at compile time.
statement: Every record in a pinned graph must carry the scope id the graph claims, on export and import alike

description: Applied at both readings: the claim's own type and the evidence records behind it. Proven exhaustively over all six evidence types, with a second proof that the SpeculationMarker vocabulary names exactly the non-positive set in both directions. The evidence-side call is currently unreachable as a rejection path because the claim-side check fires first; it stays as the binding of the second reading. Supersedes imported rules PROV-IDEATE-014 and PROV-IDEATE-016, which asked that every participant claim be labelled by evidence type and that an unsupported or exploratory recommendation never be stated as product truth.
statement: is_positive_evidence_type accepts every evidence type except unsupported and exploratory; speculation can never back an asserted claim

description: Those are outcomes of human decisions, not authorable claims. Proven exhaustively over all 28 state x link cases. Reachability differs by caller: the batch landing path and file validation hit it fully; the aggregate path guards it behind an already-proposed check for shipped-v1 tolerance; the CLI create path hard-codes legal values. The dead contradiction in proposal_from_input is tracked in beads.
statement: A modern proposal is written as proposed and nothing else, and may not carry its own duplicate-of or superseded-by verdict

description: The promotion_state column on a proposal row is a claim, not a verdict. A row that has already left proposed is frozen at what it claims; otherwise a human disposition decides (accepted, rejected, deferred); otherwise a recorded assertion makes the proposal asserted. Every proposal read applies this, so no caller sees a raw claim once lifecycle records exist. Proven exhaustively over all 56 classification cases. Supersedes imported rule PROV-IDEATE-020, which asked for a promotion-state lifecycle of proposed, accepted, rejected, deferred, duplicate, and superseded, with only accepted proposals changing a canonical record.
statement: effective_proposal_state returns the disposition's verdict when a human disposed the proposal, asserted when evidence exists, and the row's claim otherwise

description: Whole-graph semantics: any cycle in the builds-on graph rejects the batch, and the error names the proposal where the walk closed, not the full path. Diamonds and shared ancestors are not cycles. Verified by property over generated DAGs with injected cycles against an independent reachability oracle.
statement: A proposal may not, through the assertions it builds on, end up building on itself

description: The undisposed precondition reads the projected state, not the row's stored claim. Reported reasons are never fabricated: every evidence path was both cited and touched, every territory reason equals the proposal's own target. The two live paths currently disagree on which triggers they can fire (tracked in beads).
statement: An undisposed proposal surfaces to a worker exactly when the work touches a file it cited or lands on the artifact it targets

name: No project management labels
description: Imported from the Statesman era and rewritten 2026-08-10 for this product: the decision stands, only the product name changed. Prose, not a bound rule - nothing enforces it beyond the parser having no field to put such a label in, where an unknown field warns.
statement: An annotation carries no epic, feature, or story label: the requirement tree holds the hierarchy, and a rule's place in it is read from its graph chain rather than restated in source.

name: Simple key-value comment syntax
description: Rewritten 2026-08-10: the marker is @provenance; @statesman survives as a legacy alias so annotations written before the rename keep working, warned once per block rather than once per line. Prose, not a bound rule; the deciding code is parse_annotations in crates/provenance-scanner/src/parser.rs.
statement: An annotation is a @provenance key: value directive inside a comment - no function-call syntax, no parentheses, no quotes - and the legacy @statesman marker is still read, warned about once per comment block.

name: Rule field is the only required annotation
description: Rewritten 2026-08-10 against the shipped parser. The old wording claimed name is inferred from the function; it is not - the scanner records the enclosing function separately as function_name and leaves name empty unless the annotation says one. An unreadable or out-of-range confidence warns and keeps the default rather than being clamped, which is rule_confidence_range's annotation channel.
statement: rule: is the only directive that creates an annotation; name, description, tags, coverage, confidence, intent, and verification are optional, with coverage defaulting to full and confidence to 1.0.

name: Function-scoped by default with file-level override
description: Rewritten 2026-08-10 against the shipped walker. The old wording promised file-scoped annotations covering every test in a file and function-level overrides of them; neither was built. scan_file looks ahead at most six lines for a declaration and records no function name when it finds none.
statement: An annotation block binds to the first function declared in the six lines that follow it; there is no file-level annotation scope.

name: Multi-rule via separate rule lines
description: Rewritten 2026-08-10 for the marker name; the shared-then-override reading is what parse_annotations does - a field lands on the last rule named, or on the block's shared defaults while no rule has been named yet.
statement: One comment block may name several rules with one rule: line each; a field written before the first rule line applies to every rule in the block, and a field written after a rule line applies only to that rule.

name: Directives bind only on comment lines
description: Reactivated and rewritten 2026-08-10, then amended the same day when the binding lexer landed. Directives no longer bind anywhere on the line; the lexer gates on comment lines, so a marker after code on the same line is skipped. This is deliberate: trailing positions were where markers embedded in code and string lines produced false hits. The rule was originally deprecated in favour of the tree-sitter reversal (PROV-SCAN-010) that was never built and has now been deleted.
statement: The scanner reads a file only when its extension names one of the six supported languages (extensions rs, py, js, jsx, ts, tsx, java, go) and reads a directive only from a comment line: after leading whitespace the line must start with //, /*, or * (or # in Python), or continue an open block comment. A marker trailing code on the same line does not bind.

name: Line-oriented parser only
description: Reactivated 2026-08-10 as the honest owner of this decision. PROV-SCAN-010 deprecated it in favour of tree-sitter with statically linked grammars; that was never built, the shipped scanner walks lines, and both the tree-sitter rule and its resolution have been deleted. Prose, not a bound rule; the deciding code is scan_file in crates/provenance-scanner/src/walker.rs.
statement: The scanner is a line-oriented text parser with comment-prefix awareness: it does not parse ASTs, resolve imports, execute tests, or modify source code.

name: Closed relation vocabulary
description: The #[derive(Relations)] macro in crates/provenance-macros/src/relations.rs is the rule. Each StableId field on a source, requirement, resolution, rule, topic, question, or boundary carries a #[relation(target, flow, required)] attribute, or #[relation(none)] for a field that is not a relation; a StableId field with neither refuses to compile (the trybuild cases under crates/provenance-core/tests/compile_fail). The derive writes each kind's RELATIONS table, declared_relations() in crates/provenance-core/src/model/relations.rs is the one hand-written concatenation of the seven tables and the anchor of this rule, and the front in relations/front.rs derives neighbours, flows, and the projection's relations rows from those tables alone. Two tests hold the vocabulary closed: relation_tables compares every derived table against a hand-written list of the twenty declarations, and relation_walk walks each record kind's serialized fields and refuses one that no declaration names.
statement: Each reference field on a canonical record carries one relation declaration. Every reverse lookup, validator check, gap, walk, and projection row derives from that declaration.

name: Scan-time stale annotation validation
description: Validation reports markers that cite absent Rule ids as unknown ids. Current bindings to deprecated or archived Rules remain governed findings under the binding policy.
statement: The --validate-rules option checks each annotation and each #[rule] or #[verifies] attribute against the Rules in the scope. A marker citing an id with no record produces an unknown-id warning. A marker citing a deprecated or archived Rule produces a warning that names its status.

name: JSON scanner output format
description: Rewritten 2026-08-10 against CoverageReport in crates/provenance-core/src/coverage.rs. The old wording named project_id, scanned_at, and tests_found, none of which exist: the report is pinned by commit, counts annotations rather than tests, and carries the attribute bindings the cloud format had no place for.
statement: A coverage scan produces one JSON report: commit, files_scanned, total_annotations, a warnings array, an annotations array (rule id, file, line, function, coverage, confidence), and a bindings array (rule id, file, line, item, verification method).

description: Crash residue is reported for operator choice, never silently adopted or deleted - proven over all 128 output-kind x artifact-residue states with the output and residue asserted byte-for-byte untouched after every refusal (unix; Windows keeps the reparse-point example). The five artifact names are minted once in ArtifactLeaves. Amended 2026-08-10: a refusal now names every residue artifact present in role order, and an unsafe lock is a fact about a listed path rather than an early refusal hiding the rest.
statement: Publishing refuses to start when the output is not a real directory or when leftover artifacts from an interrupted run are present

description: The decision is seven facts evaluated in one function: the must path (a qualified proposal cannot be left unasserted) reads all seven from records; the may path (an assertion is allowed) passes three as witnessed by the assertion record itself. Proven over all 128 fact assignments, with every refusal blaming a genuinely unmet fact. Replaced a drifted inline copy in swarm-backtrace preflight that rejected runs the store would accept.
statement: A synthesis packet qualifies a proposal for assertion only when it owns the proposal's target, adjudicates that proposal and no other, and the proposal's cited claims stand uncontested with no blocking gap and no pending human decision

description: The serial and digest are the latest projection_revision row and the instance id is the projection_instance row. Serials compare only within one instance. The policy is the freshness step the reader ran, or catch_up_failed. The eight SDK operations answer through one reader entry, so no operation answers without a stamp.
statement: Every query answer carries a stamp that names serial, digest, instance id, derivation, policy, attested, and live
source_document: Resolution res_stamp_names_projection_instance: The wire stamp names the projection instance

statement: A query answer stops at the limit and says has_more

description: Record, byte and traversal bounds must prevent whole-scope materialization as a pagination implementation. A page exposes continuation or an explicit budget refusal.
statement: The shared query engine bounds each page before transport serialization.

description: The snapshot begins a transaction on one pooled connection and reads the latest projection_revision row and the projection_instance row first. The cache runs in WAL mode, so every row read later in the transaction is at that serial, and a publication that commits meanwhile is a later serial.
statement: A read answers from one read transaction pinned at the revision it reads first

description: Under catch_up the reader takes the guard, opens the pool inside it, runs one catch-up pass, and drops the guard before it answers. Under annotate_only no guard is taken. A canonical write therefore never waits on an open read, and a read never queues behind a publication.
statement: A read holds the publication guard for the freshness step only
source_section: E. Reader entry, Steps and Consistency

statement: A query opens the stored projection as an immutable image when permissions prevent an ordinary database open.

description: The choke point where a stored line becomes a record guards every family - a hand-edited version-2 row fails list, check, and export instead of loading silently. A line with no schema_version makes no claim and is left to its own deserializer; cross-scope edges are filtered before the guard so another scope's future data stays ignored rather than fatal. Known residual: StateStore::manifest() is still unguarded (tracked in beads). Amended 2026-08-10: the write path bypassed this guard - jsonl::mutate_jsonl_locked read shards with plain serde and no version check, so a create beside a hand-edited version-2 row re-serialised it from the fields the current struct recognised and dropped the rest, laundering into the supported layout the record every reader refuses. That read now calls the same guard on the same raw JSON before any mutation, so a refusal leaves the shard byte-identical; the exhaustion proof runs all three loaders. Remaining unguarded readers of stored content, all non-lossy Value round-trips: merge's reader, the import scope-writer's edge re-read, and StateStore::manifest().
statement: A stored record claiming an unsupported schema version is refused before it becomes a record, on the read path and on the read every write is built on, naming the file, line, record, and both versions

description: The submitted comment appears below the comment entry area against the selected record. Each top-level comment has its own reply discussion, which can be resolved independently. These interactions use the existing record-linked discussion and lifecycle behaviour.
statement: Comments submitted for a selected record are added to that record’s thread.

description: Each displayed record has a comment icon. Activating it selects the record and opens its comment surface. The discussion target remains clear while the person writes.
statement: A record comment control opens its discussion with that record selected.

description: Replies remain grouped with their starting comment. Several discussions can coexist on the same record. The storage representation remains open; this does not select multiple canonical active Threads for one record.
statement: Each top-level comment on a record has a separate reply thread.

description: At a fixed viewport, deeper records retain the reading width of their ancestors. Section headings, fold controls, relation labels and navigation can express hierarchy without cumulative indentation. Responsive layout can change width with the viewport.
statement: The document content width does not decrease as record depth increases.

description: Absence counts as a value a side can hold: identical changes are kept once, a delete against an untouched record wins silently, and a delete against an edit keeps the surviving side and reports delete_modify. Add/add with different content reports its own add_add kind, and conflicts carry the base pre-image. Proven exhaustively over all 14 reachable (base, ours, theirs) cases. Amended 2026-08-10: the driver is wired via .gitattributes, a conflicted merge exits non-zero so git falls back to conflict, and merged edge shards are validated against the endpoint table before writing - the merge no longer launders records past the write gate.
statement: merge_records keeps the moved side when only one side of a merge moved a record, and keeps ours and reports the clash when both moved differently

description: row then from_row give a record whose serde_json text equals the original, for every kind, with every field filled and with every optional field empty. The store reads each column by its storage class, never by trying an integer first, so a confidence of one stays a real.
statement: A record written to its projection row reads back as the same JSON
source_document: Resolution res_projection_tables_mirror_record_types: Projection tables mirror the record types

description: The eight kind tables and the three integration tables (implementation_bindings, verification_bindings, requirement_reviews) mirror the Rust record types, with columns named as the fields. List and struct fields are JSON text, confidence is REAL, and a bool is 0 or 1. A kind table adds one derived column, search_text. A struct field with no column fails the drift gate until its migration lands.
statement: Each record table has one column for each field of its record type
source_document: Resolution res_projection_tables_mirror_record_types: Projection tables mirror the record types

description: The person can change placement after creation as well as in the creation dialog. Use valid existing relations for the record type. Retain the discussion origin when changing placement. This does not select storage or synchronization mechanics.
statement: A record update permits selection of another compatible attachment through fuzzy search.

description: One comparison - resolved candidate equals container/name - rejects dot-dot traversal and symlinks at once, and callers may only act on the returned resolved path. An already-gone mode skips the leaf probe when nothing remains on disk. Tightened at conversion: a leaf symlink at a sibling inside the transactions directory was previously accepted. create_real_directory is the ancestor half (the cache itself is real), cross-referenced, not folded. Amended 2026-08-10: the touched leaf must also be a real directory - a regular file named by a marker is refused up front rather than failing inside removal.
statement: Recovery touches a directory only when it resolves to a real direct child of the repository cache's transactions directory

description: Gates all three read verbs; a refused reference fails every verb identically and names the mismatched field. Every mismatch arm has a direct test; exhaustion is deliberately not claimed because the input is unbounded git state. Known gap tracked in beads: exact-export documents are not self-verifying.
statement: A graph reference is honoured only if its commit exists here, the repository identity matches, the graph at that commit hashes to the recorded digest, and the id is the hash of exactly those parts

description: Version 1; grf1_/git1_ identities of exactly 64 lowercase hex; the fixed .provenance/state store path; a scope id ScopeId accepts; a full 40- or 64-character lowercase commit id, never an abbreviation; a sha256: digest; a correlation with both parts filled if present. A JSON Schema replica exists in the cli schema handler; a conformance test pushes 59 boundary values through both and asserts agreeing verdicts. One known divergence (schema_version 1.0) is tracked in beads.
statement: GraphReference::validate refuses any reference whose fields deviate from the issued shape

description: The refusal names the stored serial, revision digest, and instance id. Moved units are sorted by name. A new scope has no stored digest, and a departed scope has no live digest.
statement: The refuse_stale policy refuses changed units with their stored and live digests.

description: The hash step uses the same digest calculation as catch-up. It parses no shard records, runs no validator, and changes no projection rows. A current projection answers at the checked serial.
statement: The refuse_stale policy writes no projection revision.

description: Withdrawal ends the pending review of the candidate. It preserves feedback and decision history. Removal or retirement of the graph record requires a separate action.
statement: The agent responds to rejection by revising the proposed item or withdrawing it from review.
A contradicts pair is settled by a resolution only when the named resolution exists and was not rejected

description: The rejection comment can explain a correction or why the item is unwanted. A separate correction action is not required.
statement: A reviewer can reject a new item with or without a comment.
Rejection or withdrawal does not remove or retire the graph record.

description: One concern on a record can be resolved while another remains open. This action does not imply approval of the parent record or creation of a Rule or Resolution. Reuse of the existing Question and Thread lifecycles requires a model design.
statement: Resolving a reply thread leaves other reply thread statuses unchanged.

description: The builder gathers the facts that the source scan, the committed graph records and the evidence diff already compute. A fact those layers cannot supply stays absent from the envelope; the renderer states not supplied for it. The builder never fabricates a verification run, a pass, a commit, a complete scan or a compatible baseline. When the scan cannot pin to the head commit or the base graph cannot be compared, the envelope says incomplete or incompatible and states the reason.
statement: The envelope producer writes only facts from the repository scan and the graph. It does not invent verification evidence or completeness.
source_document: Ben: approved next slice of the deterministic pull request report track, bead provenance-4uoo, 12 September 2026

description: Graph statements, ids, paths and reasons are data. The renderer escapes them so report text cannot produce a mention, raw HTML, a link, an image, a code fence, an extra table column or a workflow command. A repository link is built only from an immutable commit and a validated repository-relative path; a complete author-supplied URL is never a trusted repository link. Text beyond the character budget is cut and the cut is stated.
statement: Untrusted envelope text cannot create markup in the report
source_document: Proposed Provenance pull request feedback research (Astra), 11 September 2026

description: The renderer sorts records, relationships, findings and evidence sites before rendering, so input order and graph shard order never change the output. The text carries no wall-clock time, run-specific random value or machine path unless the envelope supplies a value that belongs in the visible contract. The renderer treats graph statements as escaped data, uses a fixed vocabulary of sentence templates, and takes prescribed next actions from a reviewed diagnostic-code catalog in code. A renderer that calls a language model or reads conversational history breaches this Rule.
statement: Equivalent report envelopes render byte-identical Markdown
source_document: Proposed Provenance pull request feedback research (Astra), 11 September 2026

description: The badge must not let resolved lie: plain Resolved appears exactly when a decision or rule stands behind the requirement, and the admission appears exactly when none does. Non-resolved statuses never gain the suffix. Proven over every status with the count axes bucketed to zero, one, and many.
statement: A resolved requirement with no decisions and no rules is labelled Resolved (no decisions or rules), never plain Resolved

description: Blank means empty or whitespace; refused, never repaired. Enforced at deserialization via a wire-shape TryFrom, so the CLI create path and import share one gate. The reference is deliberately not resolved against the graph - it may cite legislation, a file, or a conversation the graph will never see; the rule decides something was named, not that it exists.
statement: A resolution input's reference and summary must not be blank; a field that names nothing locates nothing
resolve_symbol scans the named file alone, so the scan limit never applies to it

name: Retired bindings excluded from active views
statement: Active coverage, stale, plan, and wiki views exclude retired bindings. Export, import, check, and graph references preserve them
A query answers a retired record only when the request sets include_retired

description: Ancestors remain available as references or breadcrumbs. Canonical refinement direction determines nesting.
statement: A viewed Requirement does not place its ancestors beneath itself.

name: Only a later run clears review
statement: A verification run clears only reviews raised before it ran. Clearing writes the run and the time onto the record and keeps the reason

description: A Rule or other non-Requirement record can be expanded or selected without being submitted as a Requirement root.
statement: A nested record remains reachable when its display depth is limited.

description: Unloaded records and discussions remain distinct from empty results. A revision restart or failed catch-up is explicit.
statement: An incomplete document does not appear complete.

name: One review record per affected rule
statement: A requirement statement change writes one review record per produced rule, naming the field, its value before and after, and the change time

description: Retirement eligibility is applied before membership expansion and citation collection. Historical identity checks remain possible.
statement: Retired records do not add members or citations to an active document.

description: A matcher over loaded browser records alone cannot claim complete search coverage.
statement: Review search uses the shared search operation.
The review page calls Rust operations through the generated HTTP client.
Rust operations control persistent changes requested by the review page.

description: The agent submits the revised item to the reviewer again. Revision alone does not approve it.
statement: An item revised after rejection returns to the reviewer for a new decision.

name: A run retires only the key it reports
statement: A verification run retires only a binding whose owner, file, and key it reports against a different rule. Absence from a run retires nothing, and no run retires another owner's binding

name: Canonical Rust authored documents
statement: The Rust authoring kernel orders sources and requirements by key and rules by serialized address with lexicographic UTF-8 byte order.

name: Pure Rust authoring kernel
description: The kernel can use pure core types and functions. It cannot read process or repository state.
statement: Rust authoring build and materialize operations perform no file, environment, process, clock, repository, scanner, or store access.

name: Scan bindings after relocation
statement: The workspace-wide Rule binding scan runs after CLI SDK operations move to provenance-store.

name: Trim Rust build-time text
statement: Rust build-time content checks reject text that is empty after trimming, matching TypeScript requireText behavior.

name: Audit before Rust crate publication
statement: Rust crate publication starts only after the DR10 audit is complete and Ben records a separate go decision.

name: Capture plan goldens before relocation
statement: Rendered-plan goldens are captured before CLI SDK operations move to provenance-store.

name: Recheck Cargo artifact dependencies
statement: Rust SDK Plan work does not rely on Cargo artifact dependencies until primary-source evidence has been checked again.

name: Recheck stable const string assertions
statement: Rust SDK Plan work does not rely on compile-time key assertions until stable Rust support for const string comparison and assertion is verified.

name: Semantics-free Rust facade
statement: The provenance-sdk facade delegates materialization, structural validation, address construction, identity, planning, and mutation to provenance-core or provenance-store.

name: Store-owned persistent identity
description: Id resolution includes local-to-shared migration, ownership checks, explicit-id validation, and resolution-dependent collision checks.
statement: Only provenance-store determines persistent declaration identity.

name: Store-owned Rust symbol resolution
statement: Only provenance-store resolves an implementation symbol to a repository file for Rust SDK apply.

name: Refuse unresolved Rust symbols
statement: Rust SDK apply writes no state when an implementation symbol does not resolve to exactly one repository file.

name: Round-trip Rust typed input
statement: A Rust TypedSpec input round trip preserves every present field and the existing omission behavior.

name: Record Rust verification failure first
statement: When a Rust verification callback returns an error or unwinds, verification records the run as failed before it propagates the callback failure.

name: Stable typed-spec wire acceptance
statement: A protocol-4 typed-spec document receives the same accept-or-reject result after kernel extraction as it received before extraction.

name: Stable first wire error
statement: For a typed-spec document with more than one defect, kernel extraction preserves the first engine error class and text.

name: Preserve decoded wire order
statement: Wire ingestion returns resources and diagnostics in decoded document order and does not apply authored-document canonical ordering.
The file scan behind impact keeps the first files of a sorted walk up to the configured count

description: A later version means a different layout that today's structs would half-read silently. One function guards the five core sites with byte-identical messages; the store's four sibling copies and the unguarded non-ideation read path are tracked in beads. Proven exhaustively over five kinds x versions 0, 1, 2, and u32 max.
statement: Ideation records are read only at schema version one

description: OpenAPI generates the repetitive operation bindings. This rule does not select an OpenAPI authoring tool or remove language-specific authoring helpers.
statement: Generated SDK operation methods and wire types derive from the OpenAPI contract.
source_section: U3-U4 and A4: OpenAPI for broad client generation. U8-A8-U9: accepted generated HTTP SDK direction.

description: This constrains application call sites. Repository context and operations that require local files still need precise definitions.
statement: Changing the configured endpoint between local and hosted servers preserves the public SDK operation methods.
source_section: U5: no change to client APIs between local and cloud. U8-U9: one HTTP API.

description: The configuration API and credentials are not specified here.
statement: An explicit local SDK endpoint overrides the default local endpoint.

name: No install-time binary fetch
statement: Installing a supported SDK selects a package-manager artifact for the host and does not download an executable from an install script

description: localhost:42069 illustrates the intended default. The exact host spelling and port remain examples. This Rule does not start or install a server.
statement: A generated SDK uses a default loopback endpoint for a local target without an explicit endpoint.

name: Package supplies engine
statement: When no explicit development override is configured, an SDK resolves and runs the engine supplied for its supported host by that language package

name: Project discovery
statement: When repository configuration is omitted, SDK operations use the nearest enclosing Provenance project or Git worktree root

name: Protocol handshake before mutation
statement: An SDK rejects an engine outside its supported protocol range before sending a state-changing command

description: The owning Effect waits for request cleanup. The client aborts transport work and cancels response reading when the read is interrupted.
statement: An interrupted SDK read releases its HTTP request resources.
source_document: Bead provenance-7pkm, user dispatch of 11 September 2026
source_section: Acceptance criterion 4 and Scenario: Interrupt a read

statement: Attaching one Rule declaration to several Requirements materializes one canonical Rule with a relationship to each Requirement

description: The type name for a recorded decision is Resolution. Visible type labels and their accessible names preserve the existing ontology. Ordinary prose can still describe a decision.
statement: Record type labels in the shared view use existing Provenance type names.

description: Include records that cite the Source and records whose intent depends on it through the graph. Approval of the earlier source basis does not approve the changed basis. Automated verification alone cannot satisfy the human approval requirement. The exact dependency traversal and lifecycle representation remain design work. Withdrawn from this work after Ben clarified that existing Provenance lifecycle behaviour must remain unchanged. See res_shared_document_reuses_existing_lifecycle.
statement: A Source change requires human reapproval of every dependent record.

description: A source pin locates; a reference commit identifies. The strict shape (exactly 40 or 64 lowercase) deliberately lives in rule_reference_wellformed - two rules sharing the word commit, split on purpose, not drift. Verified by property against a written-out character-set oracle.
statement: A source commit pin is 7 to 64 hexadecimal characters, any case

description: Use the source replacement relationship to identify the affected intent. Merely linking to an old source version does not complete the revision obligation. This Rule does not specify that every statement must change wording; the review and revision procedure remains to be defined. Withdrawn from this work after Ben clarified that existing Provenance lifecycle behaviour must remain unchanged. See res_shared_document_reuses_existing_lifecycle.
statement: Replacing a Source requires revision of every record that depends on the replaced Source.

description: A projection table is readable only through a snapshot handle, and taking the handle records the table's family word. The relations table records the word relations. The stamp is built by consuming the context, so nothing reads after stamping and the list cannot omit a table.
statement: The attested list of a stamp names every projection table the read opened

description: The words are a closed list: canonical, scanned_sites, verification_runs, and diff. Each live part is reachable only through a handle taken with ReadContext::live, which records the word. A stamp never implies freshness for anything it does not list.
statement: The live list of a stamp names every part of the answer the projection does not cover
source_section: D. Stamp semantics, Wire shape and Per-operation table

name: Sound contracted verb forms
description: The finite matcher covers negative contractions and positive forms whose subject and suffix establish a contracted verb. It omits forms that need grammar or meaning choices, so a clean report does not establish complete Rule 4.2 coverage. An indeterminate quote model produces no strict finding.
statement: An exact quote model reports each recognized contracted verb outside quoted text as a Rule 4.2 violation at its UTF-8 byte span
source_section: Issue 9, Rule 4.2, pages 1-4-3 to 1-4-4 and Rule 8.6, page 1-8-7

name: Descriptive sentence length
statement: A descriptive sentence with a determinate count above 25 words produces one Rule 6.3 finding for its complete UTF-8 byte span

name: Explicit quotation counting
statement: A mechanically delimited quotation counts as one word in its containing sentence

name: Hyphenated group counting
statement: A hyphenated word or hyphenated group counts as one word

name: Number counting
statement: A mechanically identifiable number counts as one word when no Rule 8.6 meaning choice affects it

name: Ordinary colon continuity
statement: A colon in ordinary prose remains inside the descriptive sentence that contains it

name: Paragraph sentence limit
statement: When paragraph and sentence boundaries are clear, a paragraph with more than six sentences produces one Rule 6.6 finding for its full UTF-8 span

name: Parenthetical counting
statement: Parenthesized text counts once in its containing sentence and its contents count as a separate sentence

name: Quoted text protection
description: Balanced nonnested pairs produce exact protected spans. A malformed, nested, or mixed double-quote structure makes quote-dependent strict checks indeterminate.
statement: Text inside a balanced pair of straight or curly double quotation marks produces no strict Rule 4.2 or Rule 8.1 finding

name: Indeterminate semantic count
statement: A sentence with a Rule 8.6 meaning choice produces no strict Rule 6.3 finding

name: No semicolons in descriptive text
description: An indeterminate quote model produces no strict finding.
statement: An exact quote model reports each semicolon outside quoted text as a Rule 8.1 violation at its UTF-8 byte span
source_section: Issue 9, Rule 8.1, page 1-8-1 and Rule 8.6, page 1-8-7

statement: Statement analysis checks only new Requirement and Rule records and records whose statement bytes differ from the comparison base

name: Onboarding STE dictionary acquisition
description: Init can use the direct official asset. It does not need a person to complete a request form, and a selected local PDF file replaces the download.
statement: Onboarding downloads the official PDF when the project has no imported Issue 9 dictionary

name: STE asset fallback
description: The downloader stops after the fixed number of attempts. The warning names rerun init and the dictionary import command with a local PDF file. It does not search for another asset.
statement: If the official PDF asset is unavailable, onboarding prints a warning with the retry path and completes without a dictionary
source_section: Request a copy of ASD-STE100 Issue 9

name: Credit the STE stewards
description: The request page is the primary public acquisition link. The direct asset is an agent onboarding implementation detail.
statement: Product text credits ASD as owner, identifies STEMG as maintainer, and links to the official request page
source_document: STEMG ASD-STE100 copyright and legal notice

name: Link likely STE defects
description: This gives a user the steward's supported route for a proposed dictionary correction.
statement: A likely dictionary defect report includes the official STEMG change-form link

name: Limit STE product claims
description: Provenance does not claim certification, affiliation, official status, or full ASD-STE100 conformance.
statement: Product text names only the implemented Issue 9 checks and makes no compliance or endorsement claim

name: Share concurrent STE downloads
description: A lock prevents concurrent setup commands from requesting duplicate copies of the same asset.
statement: Concurrent agent onboarding commands share one download of the same Issue 9 PDF

name: Identify the STE downloader
description: The steward can identify the client and its released version from a server request.
statement: Each official PDF request identifies Provenance and its version in the HTTP User-Agent header

name: Bound STE download retries
description: A failed setup reports the failure after a configured retry bound. It does not repeatedly request the source.
statement: The official PDF downloader stops after a fixed number of failed attempts

name: Separate STE dictionary findings
description: A word can be approved only for a specified meaning and part of speech. Technical terms are not in the general dictionary.
statement: Dictionary checks report approved, unapproved, unknown, and uncertain uses as different result categories
source_section: Dictionary meanings, parts of speech, and technical terms

name: Record STE import identity
description: These values identify both the input and the extraction result without putting either data set in project configuration.
statement: Each imported dictionary records its Issue number, source digest, extracted-data digest, and extractor version

name: Reuse imported STE dictionary
description: The project records enough information to find and validate the imported dictionary. Normal checks use that local data.
statement: A project reuses its imported dictionary for later checks and does not download the PDF during each CI run

description: The index file holds extracted dictionary data outside distributed files. A load recomputes the digest over the stored entries and compares it with the identity record. A mismatch fails closed and the caller must import the PDF again. This makes rule_ste_dictionary_import_reuse safe against corrupt or edited index files.
statement: A stored dictionary index loads only when its recomputed data digest equals the recorded extracted-data digest

name: Interactive STE dictionary acquisition
description: The user completes the official human download flow. Provenance imports the selected Issue 9 PDF after the download.
statement: Interactive onboarding directs the user to the official request form and imports the PDF that the user selects
